headline: Every pack of butter checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to your dairy
heroLede: Del Bocia makes butter in Melbourne in eight varieties, from unsalted and salted to truffle, crispy chilli and anchovy, sold in 250 g packs. With that many flavours going into the same pack, the label is what keeps a fish allergen out of a plain butter fridge. This is what a camera check could look like on a butter line like yours. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every pack is wrapped and closed, with no open folds or torn corners. A loose wrap lets butter pick up fridge flavours and comes back as a complaint.
labelLede: Salted and anchovy butter look the same in the pack, but anchovy contains fish, an allergen that must be declared. The camera checks every pack carries the right label for the variety, straight and intact.
codeLede: The best-before code has to be right and readable on every pack. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the variety and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Foil offcuts, glove pieces and bits of packaging are all close at hand at packing. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four folds not tucked in fifteen minutes. Check the wrapper.
